title: Tenant traffic governor and granular fairness controller
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Summary:
Implement a runtime-integrated Tenant Traffic Governor (TTG) and Granular Fairness Controller (GFC) for Dedicated capacity that enforces throughput commitments, applies graceful backpressure on noisy tenants, and cooperates with the autoscaler to preserve SLOs. The TTG will operate as a distributed token-bucket + credit borrowing system with admission controls that understand model footprint (GPU time / memory) and priority classes.

Goals:
- Guarantee committed throughput for reservation customers while allowing controlled burst/flex on unused capacity.
- Limit noisy-neighbor cost and latency impact on co-tenants via transparent throttling and soft preemption policies.
- Integrate with autoscaling signals so capacity growth/eviction decisions respect tenant contracts and fairness windows.
- Provide observability (per-tenant tokens, borrow usage, throttled-rates, retry-after histograms) and an operator playbook for incident response.

Design highlights:
1) Token-bucket governor per tenant: replenishment rate is derived from the tenant's committed throughput (tokens per second). Tokens represent normalized GPU-token-cost units (computed from a model footprint table). Requests consume tokens based on model, sequence length, and concurrency estimate.
2) Grace credits: tenants may borrow up to a configurable short-term credit budget (in seconds of equivalent throughput). Borrowing accrues a debt metric used by the fairness controller.
3) Fairness controller: periodically (1s window) computes a fairness score across tenants on the node/pool and applies proportional dampening to borrowed budgets when contention exceeds thresholds. The controller also supports emergency soft-preemption of best-effort workloads.
4) Autoscale handshake: when node-level soak or pressure events are detected, the governor sends an autoscale advisory signal (per-tenant demand curve + borrow pressure). The autoscaler uses this to prioritize capacity adds and informed preemption candidates.
5) Admission responses: for requests that cannot be admitted due to token exhaustion, the runtime returns a 429 with a Retry-After, or optionally queues short requests when latency SLOs allow. The response contains transparent diagnostic headers for the SDK to surface.
6) Config model: operator controls for committed rate, grace budget, borrow-pricing (penalty multiplier), priority class, and eviction score weights.

Trade-offs and risks:
- Strict enforcement improves isolation but increases throttled errors for bursty customers; grace credits mitigate but complicate billing semantics.
- Integrating with autoscale adds coupling between bandwidth enforcement and capacity decisions — will need robust testing to avoid churn loops.
- Per-request footprint computation adds CPU overhead; we cache typical footprints per model/shape to reduce cost.

Implementation plan (milestones):
- Week 1–2: Prototype in runtime-local mode that simulates token consumption and exposes test hooks (ENG-130998-pt1).
- Week 3: Integrate fairness controller and simulated borrow scenarios with unit tests and load harness.
- Week 4: Autoscaler advisory API and end-to-end test on a canary pool; add diagnostic headers in SDK.
- Week 5: Observability dashboards and SLO regression tests; security review.
- Week 6: Canary rollout to small Dedicated fleet slice, gather metrics and customer beta.

Rollout and canary plan:
- Canary pool with strict monitoring: CPU/GPU utilization, throttled-rates, tail latency by tenant, borrow-debt growth.
- Beta cohort: 3 customers (one with guaranteed commit, one bursty best-effort, one mixed) with clear rollback criteria.

Observability artifacts and links:
- Design doc (internal Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/TTG+Design+Doc
- Autoscale RFC: https://docs.redwood.ai/rfc/autoscale-handshake-2026
- Load harness dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/ttg-load/ttg-canary
- Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1426

Operational playbook (short):
- If throttled-rate spikes and LLQ borrow debt > 80%: move offending tenant to temporary hard-quota and notify SE.
- If node churn increase > 5% after TTG enabled: pause borrow-enabled flag, monitor for autoscale oscillation.
- Security: tokens and advisory payloads are signed and audited; security review required before GA.

Success metrics:
- Committed SLAs met for 99th percentile latency and throughput for reservation tenants in canary pools.
- Reduction in cross-tenant latency regressions during noisy bursts vs baseline by 60%.
- No autoscale-induced capacity flapping in 95% of observed scale events.
